Relativity is building humanity’s multiplanetary future. We invented a new approach to design, build, and fly our own rockets, starting with Terran 1 – the world’s first entirely 3D printed rocket, and Terran R, our next generation medium-heavy lift reusable launch vehicle.
 
As a vertically integrated technology platform, Relativity is at the forefront of an inevitable shift toward software-defined manufacturing. By fusing 3D printing, artificial intelligence, and autonomous robotics, we are pioneering the factory of the future. Disrupting 60 years of aerospace, Relativity offers a radically simplified supply chain, building a rocket with fewer parts and faster iteration.
 
We believe in a future where interplanetary life fundamentally expands the possibilities for human experience. Our long-term vision is to upgrade humanity’s industrial base on Earth and on Mars.

launches.title: Care Weather 🌎 🛰️ Highest-accuracy global weather data from low-cost satellites
launches.tagline: We help weather-sensitive organizations adapt to increasingly extreme weather.
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We’re [Alex](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alex-laraway-8ba461169/) and [Patrick](http://linkedin.com/in/mpatrickwalton) from [Care Weather](https://www.careweather.com/). We’re leveraging SpaceX rideshare and 5G electronics to make a swarm of low-cost satellites that get 17X more accurate global weather data.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79524&key=user_uploads/349337/502dc652-58a2-489c-928c-3cedb21358be)

_(Left) Alex with with a flight-ready satellite. (Right) Patrick testing the latest satellite._

### [🌪️](https://emojipedia.org/tornado) **Problem**

Weather is quietly [costing billions](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/billions/) across the economy. For example:

* ✈️ A recent supertyphoon damaged $200M of Air Force planes in Guam ([JTWC](https://www.metoc.navy.mil/jtwc/products/atcr/2018atcr.pdf)).
* 🚢 Ocean cargo ships reroute around so many unpredicted cyclones that they lose $60M of voyage time per ship per year.

It may seem like your weather app has tons of data to prevent this, but weather apps pretend predicted data is real. Those predictions are based on limited, inaccurate measurements from aging government satellites. Other solutions (weather stations, balloons, drones) aren’t scalable.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79524&key=user_uploads/349337/5ce389df-7421-4592-aa8c-dc75b9ba0e7b)

### **🌎 🛰️ Solution**

After studying with a NASA expert, we invented a modernized radar satellite, called [Veery](https://careweather.com/tech). We can mass produce Veery at low cost and get orders of magnitude more truth data. Veery’s flat form factor gives it way more solar power and lets it sail on top of the atmosphere for a closer view of the surface. Veery will map ocean surface vector winds, soil moisture, and sea ice globally, every hour, with 100 m - 6 km resolution.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79524&key=user_uploads/349337/fe836808-1163-4870-b7d1-7849bbbadb47)

### **🚀 Traction**

In the last four months, we built and launched the smallest radar satellite in history! And we did it with pre-seed funding and a team of two. In the same timeframe, we received $50M worth of LOIs from the Air Force, the National Weather Service, and several maritime companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79524&key=user_uploads/349337/563a1d03-1716-4c5d-a467-4ad4ff993d97)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79524&key=user_uploads/349337/20167ab2-c237-4521-995e-2b2b114502c8)

### **Asks**

Help us build a disaster-free future!

* Follow us on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/CareWeather) and [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/careweather/).
* If you work with weather data or in a weather-sensitive business, [sign up for our waitlist](https://careweather.com/waitlist)! We’ll have pilot data this Fall.

name: TransAstra Corporation
long_description: With five issued patents covering our core business lines, and more than a dozen additional patents pending this year and more than $5M in revenue, TransAstra is developing the technologies that will drive the rapidly expanding space economy. Our breakthrough Omnivore propulsion system can propel spacecraft, including our Worker Bee commercial OTV with water or virtually any other fluid as a propellant using only concentrated sunlight as a power source. Omnivore is faster, cheaper, and more practical than electric propulsion while being substantially less expensive, safer, and more operationally flexible than legacy chemical propulsion systems. Our Sutter Telescope System can identify and locate resource-rich asteroids and orbital debris that existing technologies can’t find and works synergistically with our Worker Bee OTV for orbital logistics. For government customers, Sutter can identify dark fast-moving objects between Earth and the Moon which currently evade detection, a critical issue for national defense and a key need of the Space Force. We are already using Sutter in ground-based observatories and will begin commercial sales of Sutter SDA data next month having tracked dozens of faint moving objects in space already. Once launched into space, Sutter will be 300,000 times more cost effective than any other known telescope design and will revolutionize sense making in space.

launches.title: 🛰 Quindar - Automated Satellite Operations
launches.tagline: Satellite Mission Management as a Service
launches.body:
Hey everyone! **Today we’re launching** [**Quindar**](https://www.quindar.space/), **a web app used by satellite owners to track, contact, monitor and operate** **satellites from deployment into space until end-of-life.** For example, NASA could use Quindar to test and operate their satellites with minimal human intervention.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=64358&key=user_uploads/1003779/68b30bb5-43ce-4cfc-87f5-ebfafd3e3cdc)

We’re six former [OneWeb](https://oneweb.net/) engineers who helped build the software that operates the second largest satellite constellation today – at 428 and counting. After OneWeb, we built another operations center for an earth imaging constellation but today we are building a unified platform for every satellite owner.

### **The Satellite Industry Problem**

Current satellite mission software solutions are a mix of COTS products that was built over 20 years ago.

* ☁️  Not cloud native
* 🛰  Created for a handful of satellites
* 🔐  Outdated security
* 💽  Rarely web native

There are 4,500 active satellites in orbit today however **1,700 will be launched** **each year** through 2030. The space industry is shifting from companies launching a handful of satellites over a decade, to launching hundreds of satellites in just a few years.

**The traditional model of many engineers operating a few satellites doesn’t scale.**

### **The Quindar Solution**

Quindar provides satellite mission management as a service. Our platform:

* Allows only a single engineer to operate hundreds of satellites.
* Includes the software to track, contact, and monitor satellites. No installation required.
* Integrates seamlessly with AWS and Atlas antennas (more to come).
* Aggregates and analyzes satellite, antenna, and infrastructure anomalies.
* Accessible from any phone or computer.
* Built on AWS GovCloud with the latest FedRAMP and NIST security controls.

### **Why the world needs Quindar**

Our mission is to democratize space. To be the IT for what are essentially flying servers. Customers need to focus on their mission - image collection and resolution, docking to another spacecraft, landing on an asteroid, or broadband from space and let us manage the infrastructure and software utility that supports it.

### **How you can help**

**If you, your friends, or colleagues are trying to launch a satellite please reach out to us at** [**founders@quindar.space**](mailto:founders@quindar.space)**.** We’d love to save them the pain of building and managing a software team and all the gotcha’s that come with satellite ops! Friends don’t let friends build their own mission ops 🙅.

Email: [founders@quindar.space](mailto:founders@quindar.space)

Website: <https://quindar.space/>

[@Nate Hamet](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nathanhamet/), [@Matt Regan](https://linkedin.com/in/matthew-regan-a0a45238), [@David Lawrence](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-lawrence-58663691/), [@Sunny Bhagavathula](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sandilya-sunny-bhagavathula-13780b47/), [@Shaishav Parekh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shaishavparekh), Zach Meza

name: Spaceium Inc

Spaceium builds fully automated space stations to refuel and repair spacecraft. We have secured $86.1 million in binding commercial contracts and have an additional $230 million in the pipeline. Additionally, we have 1 billion dollars in letters of intent. We have successfully tested our hardware, which will launch to space next year. 

Our fully automated space stations will efficiently store and transfer both cryogenic (extremely cold) and non-cryogenic fuels with zero loss during storage and transfer. And they can transfer fuel seamlessly to any spacecraft design using our proprietary modular robotic arm.

Our customers include launch vehicles, orbital transfer vehicles, moon landers, and spacecraft that benefit from increased payload capacity and extended travel capabilities. Our long-term vision is to build service hubs along the space superhighway to connect Earth to Moon and Mars and help humanity to become multi multi-planetary species

"Helping space explorers go "where no man has gone before" - Captain James T. Kirk :)

**_ _** 

Hi, everyone. We are [Ashi Dissanayake](https://linkedin.com/in/ashi-dissanayake) and [Reza Fetanat](https://linkedin.com/in/rezafetanat), the team behind [Spaceium](https://spaceium.com/).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=81561&key=user_uploads/985204/76cbc58c-243e-410f-99ca-5eaa12bdeb79)

**Here's a brief introduction:**

**Ashi** is an Aerospace Engineer specializing in **Orbital Mechanics and rocket propulsion.** Ashi has worked on real-time simulation models for uncrewed return missions to asteroids and on **NASA-related aerodynamics projects**.

**Reza** is also a space enthusiast and a Mechanical Engineer specializing in **Robotics, structures, and Cryogenics**. Reza has worked on revitalizing the **LR-101 engine, which was used on Atlas, Thor, and Delta launch vehicles.**

We first met while leading the University of Ottawa's rocketry team, where we built high-powered rockets to send scientific payloads to different altitudes. In our spare time, we enjoyed working together to build rockets in the backyard, sometimes leading to interesting experiences with backyard fires. 🔥

Throughout our careers, we've noticed the constraints on space missions due to the lack of ability to refuel or repair spacecraft in orbit. The current solutions are costly, and a centralized location where spacecraft can refuel and repair is a massive necessity. We are on a mission to build the missing piece of space infrastructure that connects the space superhighway, Just like how service stations were built on Earth back in the day!

# **The problem**

All spacecraft and space missions face a standard set of challenges. Fuel is a limited and difficult resource to transport. In the event of a significant issue, spacecraft cannot be repaired in space. These challenges have significantly hindered efficiency in current space missions and have been a substantial obstacle in humanity's quest to explore space further. 

Unlike a road trip where refueling is common and convenient, spacecraft face a unique challenge. Spacecraft cannot refuel along the way. Instead, they must carry all the fuel required for the mission from Earth. **An overwhelming 85% - 95% of the launch weight is fuel on a typical launch vehicle, with 80-90% burned off to reach orbit.** 🚀

As a result, spacecraft that transport loads in space (space tugs) can only perform, **on average, 25% as many missions as they're technically capable of due to the absence of refueling in space.** 🛰️

Furthermore, even if a spacecraft wanted to carry additional fuel, it is not easy. Current spacecraft require cryogenic fuels such as liquid oxygen, methane, and liquid hydrogen, which must be stored and transferred at extremely low temperatures of -285°F. 🥶 Environmental factors in space, such as heat and radiation, increase the temperature of these fuels, causing them to boil off (vaporize).

In addition, **there is no current solution for spacecraft repair**. This means that today's spacecraft must operate flawlessly to maximize efficiency, which is only sometimes the case. For instance, Eutelsat Communications' satellites experienced power loss mid-mission with no option for repair, resulting in a **$30 million** revenue loss. **With Spaceium's multifunction robotic arm, the communication satellite could have been fixed.** 🛠️

# **Solution**

_Automated servicing stations in space 🌎🚀🛰️_

Our primary solution aims to improve space missions' efficiency by addressing refueling challenges. **The developed cryogenic fuel storage and transfer technology is designed to store fuel without any boil-off for multiple years in space.** As a result, spacecraft can now refuel in space, carry more payload, and travel longer distances.

Two fundamental principles guide our proprietary Zero Boil Off (ZBO) technology. 

* Firstly, we prevent heat from entering the system through a unique tank design, insulation, and coating system. 
* Secondly, our innovative multistage closed-loop cooling system evenly removes the heat from the cryogenic fuel and transfers it to radiators, ensuring zero boil-off.

 

Our cryogenic storage system is not only efficient but also highly scalable. Our current cooling system is **65% more efficient** than any other cooling system, and our scalable storage system can store up to 30 metric tons of fuel, making it adaptable to a wide range of space missions and requirements.

After successfully addressing the challenge of transporting large amounts of space fuel, we turned our attention to developing technology for delivering this fuel to spacecraft in space. This is achieved through the use of a **multifunction robotic arm**. This advanced arm can securely dock with incoming spacecraft and initiate the fuel transfer. **The fluid system built within the arm allows the transfer of different fuel types through the robotic arm**. The built-in thermal system ensures that fuel is transferred to the customer's spacecraft at the correct temperature without any boil-off issues associated with cryogenic fuels in space.

Additionally, the same robotic arm is versatile enough to handle non-cryogenic fuels as well, providing a comprehensive solution for refueling spacecraft in space.

In addition to safe and efficient fuel transfer, the robotic arm is equipped with an interchangeable end effector designed for in-space repairs. In-space repairs are achieved through a fully automated robotic arm that can retrieve tools from a stored "toolbox" within the system. This innovative feature ensures that even in the event of a significant issue, spacecraft can be repaired in space, minimizing the risk of mission failure and maximizing mission efficiency.

Our vision is to transform the space industry. Starting in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), our servicing infrastructure will progressively expand to encompass Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO), the moon, and eventually Mars. We are on a mission to empower space missions to go further, explore more, and achieve what was once deemed impossible.

**Who can benefit from our service stations in space** 

* **Launch vehicles** 
* **Orbital transfer vehicles** 
* **Space tugs** 
* **Moon landers** 
* **Satellites**

# **Ask**

* **Feedback, comments, or questions.** Reach out to us to learn how we can help with your missions.
* **Warm Intros.** If you know or work with any launch providers, space companies, or satellite providers who could benefit from our service, please introduce us to them. 🛰 
* **Follow.** Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/spaceium-inc), [X](https://x.com/SpaceiumInc). Cool news coming soon
* **Share.** Please share this post with your network so we can reach more space companies looking for refueling, repairs, and other services for their future missions. 👾

# Email us [HERE](mailto:founders@spaceium.com).

Thank you!

news.title: Instinct Space Unveils Plans for Low-Cost Lunar Landers

launches.title: Instinct - Lunar Landers as a Service
launches.tagline: lunar landers designed to launch as a regular LEO rideshares
launches.body:
We are going to the Moon, without spending billions. Launching more often and from any rocket.

### **TL;DR:**

Modern lunar landers are not designed for the realities of today's launch market, leading to infrequent and expensive flights. Instinct is building a lunar lander that can launch from anywhere, increasing flight cadence and decreasing cost.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-WG8NVonbOo>

### **The Problem:**

Demand for the Moon is increasing, and modern landers rely on dedicated launches to the Moon that cost upwards of $100M and only fly once or twice a year. This means payload costs of $1.2M/kg and very limited availability of payload slots. Most potential lunar payloads are either stuck on Earth or never leave the concept stage.

### **Our Solution:**

Instinct's lunar lander is small enough to launch as a rideshare to Low Earth Orbit, enabling low-cost, high-cadence missions. From LEO, our lander makes its way to the Moon without the need for refueling or multiple stages, delivering 20kg of payload to the Moon at a cost per kg of less than half that of current providers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103381&key=user_uploads/1741395/a31b9757-ea96-4f67-8e24-a31ef7bf474b)


At its core, our lunar lander relies on custom propulsion and visual navigation systems, which enable our unique architecture and most importantly are designed to keep vehicle mass as low as possible. This reduces launch cost and maximizes performance.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103381&key=user_uploads/1741395/6887996a-f7fc-4d07-a5ae-68e548ba6acf)

### **Who We Are:**

Our team brings years of experience working on space missions including NASA's IMAP, ESA's Solar Orbiter, and PhiSat-2.

We are super passionate about space exploration, and have also experienced firsthand the pains involved in developing lunar missions nowadays. We think getting to the Moon should be routine.

### **What's Next:**

* Integrated tests of our reaction control thrusters
* Flight of our hopper test vehicle
* A lot of testing
* First lunar mission in Q4 2028

### **Asks:**

* Fly a payload to the Moon\![ https://www.instinct-space.com/fly-with-us](https://www.instinct-space.com/fly-with-us)
* Commercial/Government Intros
* Join the team[ https://www.instinct-space.com/careers](https://www.instinct-space.com/careers)

name: Exosat
long_description:
Exosat is building thousands of low-cost communication satellites to provide a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. By designing our satellites with zero ITAR/EAR-controlled content, we can leverage manufacturers anywhere in the world to produce our satellites at under a tenth of the cost and launch them from other nations to bypass capacity bottlenecks and access equatorial orbits. 

We're starting off by selling connectivity to device OEMs and network operators, but will eventually use the distributed compute across our constellation to run low-latency inference for robots and autonomous vehicles in remote and rural areas anywhere on the planet.

We've already signed hundreds of millions in LOIs to work with operators across Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, booked our first satellite launch next year, and hold an 11,000 satellite filing with the ITU to build the largest comms network outside of the U.S. and China.

launches.title: Exosat — Building a sovereign Starlink
launches.tagline: Building thousands of low-cost communication satellites as a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. We launch the first one next April.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Exosat is building a sovereign alternative to Starlink with thousands of low-cost satellites. We’ve booked our first launch next April and signed hundreds of millions in LOIs with customers across six nations. We’re looking to connect with operators interested in sovereign networks and AI infrastructure. Email us: [founders@exosat.com](mailto:founders@exosat.com)**

Exosat is building thousands of low-cost communication satellites to provide a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. 

We launch our first satellite **next April**, have signed **$400M in LOIs** with customers across 6 nations, and hold an ITU filing for 11,000 satellites to build the largest comms network outside of the United States and China.

[Video](https://youtu.be/aABRZfcYAFQ)

### **⏰ Problem**

Nations and enterprises are wary about depending on Starlink.

These concerns aren’t without merit. In 2022, Starlink access was suddenly cut to stop a Ukrainian counteroffensive. As a result, nations have realized that a foreign superpower owning your satellites makes you ultimately dependent on their continued permission to access it.

In Europe, telecoms are warning about the danger of relying on foreign-owned AI and satellite infrastructure:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/9dc3272a-bf85-4710-ad4d-e4592100ca1e)

In Indonesia, telecoms are lobbying for a Starlink ban:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/5596ba12-4d01-4acd-b11c-8b1e777bb663)

In India, Starlink rollout has been delayed due to security concerns:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/e4e7cd9a-e67d-42f8-bd8a-c1a78a0f4034)

And even nations like Canada are moving off of dependence on American space infrastructure:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/b73fbed9-3742-4105-8a86-de42843dbd1b)

But even if they don’t trust Starlink, that doesn’t mean they necessarily trust constellations like Qianfan or Guowang that are owned and operated by Chinese state enterprises.

However, other alternatives outside of the U.S. and China face years of delay or need millions of dollars just to build a single satellite, which leaves hundreds of millions people still without reliable connectivity. 

### **🛰️ Our Solution**

Exosat fixes this problem by building thousands of satellites at a tenth of the usual cost.

We focus entirely on civil and commercial customers outside of the United States or China and fly our satellites in lower orbits versus incumbents like AST and Iridium, enabling us to take advantage of better link budgets, faster latency, and a milder radiation environment.

These factors let us use global manufacturing hubs or local partners to build our satellites using automotive-grade parts and **zero** ITAR/EAR-controlled supply chains, enabling us to seamlessly launch from other nations to bypass capacity bottlenecks and access equatorial orbits.

As a result, we can deploy a communications satellite with a 3-5 year lifespan for **\~$300k instead of $5M** and in days instead of months, enabling us to manufacture and deploy a mega-constellation at near cost-parity to Starlink.

**Our thesis is simple: we’re building a satellite at <10% of the cost to dominate 80% of the market instead of going after everyone.**

### **👋 About Us**

I’m a second-time space founder who previously built Aethero, a company developing satellite edge computers. We scaled to millions of dollars in revenue from defense primes like Blue Origin and Booz Allen Hamilton, won multiple SBIR awards, launched two satellites to orbit, and did radiation research on GPUs with the Aerospace Corporation and AFRL.

I started Exosat and moved to Singapore because I think a future where SpaceX and China monopolize the space economy is a bleak one. I’m willing to go for broke, and put down the deposit for our first launch slot next year with my own money.

### **📈 What have we done?**

Since starting out this summer, we’ve:

* **Booked our first launch** for next April, with early pilots underway to start initial commercial service for satellite IoT no later than the end of 2028.
* **Added $400M+ in LOIs** from early customers across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Central Asia to either lease future network capacity from our dedicated constellation or build and launch their own sovereign networks with our satellites.
* **Published ITU filings to build an 11,000 satellite constellation** to build the biggest satellite network outside of the United States and China.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109889&key=user_uploads/689300/2420ddf1-1da9-4f74-b6ef-15dd51f24eb2)

### **🙏 Our Ask**

If any of these describe you or your organization, we'd love to talk:

* Network operators interested in space-based capacity
* National space agencies interested in sovereign space capabilities
* Industrial users in maritime, energy, mining, logistics, who rely on satellites for tasks such as AIS or remote connectivity
* OEMs producing satellite-connected devices and gateways

👉 Reach us at [info@exosat.com](mailto:info@exosat.com)

**Fun fact:** We’re the first YC space company to be based in Asia.

launches.tagline: Pacific mass produces micro data centers for Earth and space, faster than anyone else.
launches.body:
**Building the toughest super computers for earth and space**\
\
**TL;DR:** Data centers are stuck for years waiting for power, while delayed construction sites across the world sit on unused interconnects, losing $1B per week in the US alone, in interest on trillions of dollars of debt. Our pods deploy on those sites and generate revenue for them in days. They use diamond wafers in the cooling system so pods run anywhere on earth, even a desert.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rf8cCV6qFow>

**The deal**

If you need compute (GPU hours, tokens, capacity for a training run) send us a note. We sell short and long-term contracts below market rate.

If your data has to stay on-prem (**defense, CUI, CMMC)**, we sell managed, modular pods directly and are already working with large aerospace companies.

**We're building factories**

SpaceX didn't just build rockets, they built rocket factories. We do the same and our first factory stands up over the next few months, potentially funded by the state of Missouri. We vertically integrate the critical components that currently carry multi-year lead times: transformers, switchgear and power distribution, and by taking control of our own supply chain we ensure we can build pods fast enough.

**Financed like aircraft**

Our pods are financed like aircraft - debt at **\~5-6%, not 11-15%**. A data center is a risky construction loan: money stuck in a half-built site for years, and if it fails the lender holds a building and a pile of GPUs priced by a brutally volatile market - the banks are freaking out. Our pods leave the factory fully functional, earns the moment it's connected to power, and can be repossessed and redeployed: the profile of equipment finance, far faster and cheaper.

**Traction**

Today we have $95M in LOI’s for our hosted compute and a further $27M for direct sales of our pods. Our first two clusters go live in Missouri this month, followed by the first modular factory.

**Our asks**

* **Compute buyers and offtake.** We'd love to speak to anyone buying compute, or setting up on-prem deployments, or needing CMMC compliance. Introductions to procurement teams at OpenAI, Anthropic, or any startup constrained by access to cheap compute would be incredible.
* **Hiring.** Data center engineers, electrical engineers, any data center nerds you know.
* **Financiers.** These projects run on capital from infra investors and tech lenders. If you've worked in that world, we'd love to chat.
* **Construction sites.** If you sell to construction sites, work in construction, mining, or fab production, or own a site yourself - we will put a money machine on it. Let's chat.

**Join us as we build supercomputers for the galaxy!**
